title: Witchcraft
problem: Each Cursed enemy auto-casts a single-target damage gem through the normal auto-cast, which always aims at the caster's opponents, i.e. your creatures. It never picks a random creature from both sides. It also casts the first eligible gem, not a random one.
notes: Community claim: Never a random creature: always hits your team, even with Confused. Evidence: bc_CreatureCast L1867-L1880 @0x14077ac6a (Cursed filter 20, gem tag DAMAGE + target type 0, bc_CreatureCastSpellGem with 3 args, no target); ARTIFACTS.md § Target selection (harmful → opposing side). Fix sketch: T: "on one of your creatures". H for a truly random target Triage 2026-10-26: Ruling 2026-10-26 (stat/scope/trigger wording): text matches code. Cursed enemies always cast at your creatures. 2026-10-26: text correction shipped via localization_override (loader text module). | 2026-10-26 realign (text is the contract): text claims "cast one of their single-target damage spells on a random creature". Fix: H: Witchcraft auto-cast (bc_CreatureCast L1867-L1880 @0x14077ac6a) should pick a random gem among the eligible ones and a random living target from both sides. vs bugged: stronger for the Witchcraft user (the code always aimed the Cursed casts at your creatures). | Batch S: left needs-hook. Needs a new random-target pick over both sides inside bc_CreatureCast's targeting code; no single call site to stand in for. Round-2 C2 2026-10-26: still needs-hook; waits for batch A2's array helper. Text claims only 'on a random creature' (not a random gem). The Cursed cast goes through bc_CreatureCastSpellGem -> bc_EventCast -> bc_CreatureCast(caster, targets, gem, auto), which picks the opposing side; a fix needs either a C-built target array (random living creature from crits + enemies) passed to bc_EventCast, or a hook on the picker under a Witchcraft context flag. | 2026-10-26 hook batch F1 built (research/hooks_F1.json, loader/hooks_F1.c). Left needs-hook. The Cursed auto-cast (bc_CreatureCast L1880 @0x14077bb08) calls bc_CreatureCastSpellGem with 3 args and no target (its argc check only knows 1 / 2), so there is no call to stand in for that could pass a target; the fix needs a Witchcraft context flag around that call plus a hook in the target picker inside bc_CreatureCastSpellGem / bc_EventCast that picks a random living creature from both sides. | 2026-10-26 patched (hooks_G4, SU-0143): the Witchcraft auto-cast (bc_CreatureCast L1880, bc_CreatureCastSpellGem with no target) is flagged. At that cast's bc_EventCast (bc_CreatureCastSpellGem L288) its targets array is rewritten to one random living creature (hp > 0) from both sides (global.crits 1-6 and global.enemies 1-6, the caster excluded), picked with the game's irandom_range. If no candidate is found, the game's own targets stay. The gem choice is unchanged: the text says 'one of their' spells, which the first eligible gem satisfies. Self-targeting is excluded as a judgment call: a creature casting its damage spell on itself is not what 'a random creature' implies. In-game test: Witchcraft on several Cursed enemies; over a few turns their damage spells hit random creatures on both teams (enemies hit each other too), each cast hitting exactly one creature, never the caster and never a dead creature. 2026-10-26 user: random follows the game's pattern, which excludes the caster. Checked: the game's bc_GetRandomOtherCreature (used by the Confused redirect in bc_CreatureAttack L114 / bc_CreatureCast L225) excludes the acting creature and picks from its own party; Witchcraft's 'a random creature' spans both sides, so the patch keeps its both-sides pick with the same caster exclusion. No change. 2026-10-28: the target-list writes now pop the runtime's owner stack after each element write (0x1478957b0, 1), as the game's code does; without it, every Witchcraft cast left two entries behind (the cause of a crash to desktop found with SU-0275).

release_notes.intended: Cursed enemies cast one of their single-target damage spells on a random creature.
release_notes.actual: In the unpatched game, the spell always hit the caster's opponents.
release_notes.fix: Now the target is a random living creature from either side, other than the caster.
